title: Why Is WD-40 Company (WDFC) Stock Up +16% Today?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* WD-40 Company shares are up approximately 16% in premarket trading after a blowout fiscal third-quarter earnings report.
* The primary catalyst is a massive earnings and revenue beat, with adjusted EPS of $2.33 versus a consensus estimate of $1.58, a surprise of more than 47%.
* Revenue came in at $195.1 million, up 24% year-over-year and topping estimates by over 13%, marking one of the strongest quarterly beats in company history.
* Net income surged 44% and operating income jumped 47% from the prior-year quarter, signaling significant margin improvement.
* WD-40 shares had already gained about 25% year-to-date heading into the print, outperforming the S&P 500's roughly 9% gain.
* Traders are watching for management commentary on the earnings call regarding the sustainability of this growth and any update to full-year guidance.

# Opening Summary

WD-40 Company (WDFC) is the San Diego-based maker of the iconic WD-40 multi-use lubricant along with a broader portfolio of maintenance and cleaning products sold globally. Shares closed the prior session at $244.11 and are indicated up roughly 16% in premarket trading Friday, putting the stock near the $283 level. The move follows Thursday's release of fiscal third-quarter 2026 results, which showed net sales of $195.1 million, a 24% increase from the prior-year quarter. Markets are reacting to a sharp earnings and revenue beat that far exceeded Wall Street expectations.

# Earnings Results Drive the Rally

WD-40 reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.33 for the quarter ended May 31, 2026, crushing the Zacks consensus estimate of $1.58 by more than 47% and marking a significant jump from $1.54 per share a year earlier. Revenue of $195.12 million surpassed consensus estimates by roughly 13.6%, compared with year-ago revenue of $156.91 million. Operating income rose 47% to $40.3 million, while net income climbed 44% to $30.2 million, reflecting both stronger sales volumes and improved margins. This scale of outperformance across nearly every headline metric is the clearest driver behind the premarket surge in WDFC shares.

# Sales Growth Across Product Lines

The 24% increase in net sales reflects strength in WD-40's core maintenance products, continuing a pattern seen in recent quarters where the company has benefited from pricing actions and steady global demand for its namesake lubricant. This marks a notable acceleration from the company's fiscal 2026 guidance of just 5% to 9% full-year sales growth issued back in October, suggesting the third quarter significantly outpaced management's own expectations. The magnitude of this beat raises questions about whether full-year guidance will be revised upward on the earnings call.

# Market Context and Trading Activity

WD-40 shares had already climbed about 25% year-to-date prior to this report, comfortably outperforming the S&P 500's roughly 9% gain over the same period. A premarket move of 16% is unusually large for WDFC, a historically low-volatility consumer staples name, and is likely to come with trading volume well above the stock's typical average. The move stands in contrast to the broader Consumer Products - Staples industry, which has ranked in the bottom portion of Zacks industry rankings recently, underscoring that this rally is company-specific rather than sector-wide.

# What Comes Next for WDFC

Investors will be watching for management's commentary on the earnings call regarding the sustainability of this quarter's growth rate and any potential revision to full-year fiscal 2026 guidance, which currently calls for EPS between $5.75 and $6.15. Analysts currently hold a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), reflecting a mixed estimate revision trend heading into the print. Key risks include potential volatility in freight and input costs, currency headwinds affecting international sales, and whether the strong quarter reflects a durable trend or a temporary pull-forward in demand.
